about: Where the fixtures of tests/pack-cloud-guardduty.test.ts come from. No real export exists. The files are written by hand from the field lists of the AWS pages under 'pages', read on 2026-11-04 (read-only page reading, nothing downloaded); every value in them is invented (documentation address ranges, made-up ids, an example account). Claims below are paraphrases of what each page says; a verifier re-reads the page and checks the claim.

finding.title: Finding (GuardDuty API reference)
supports: The Finding object has accountId, arn, createdAt, id, region, resource, schemaVersion, severity, type and updatedAt (all required), and the optional associatedAttackSequenceArn, confidence, customDetectionRuleName, description, partition, service and title.
severity is a Double; createdAt and updatedAt are Strings; the type is a string of 1 to 100 characters.
The Region of a finding generated from global service events might differ from the Region where GuardDuty identifies the potential threat.

service.title: Service (GuardDuty API reference)
supports: The Service object has the optional members action, additionalInfo, archived (Boolean: whether the finding is archived), count (Integer: the total count of the occurrences of this finding type), detection, detectorId, ebsVolumeScanDetails, eventFirstSeen and eventLastSeen (Strings), evidence, featureName, malwareScanDetails, resourceRole, runtimeDetails, serviceName and userFeedback.
The page lists no member that marks a finding as archived by a suppression rule.

get-findings.title: GetFindings (GuardDuty API reference)
supports: The response is a JSON object whose findings member is an array of Finding objects (at most 50), with lowerCamelCase member names, for example accountId, createdAt, service.archived, service.count and service.eventLastSeen.
The Evidence object of the response holds threatIntelligenceDetails, a list of objects with threatFileSha256, threatListName and threatNames.

The action object of the response holds actionType and, by type, awsApiCallAction, dnsRequestAction, kubernetesApiCallAction, networkConnectionAction, portProbeAction and rdsLoginAttemptAction, among others; a network connection action holds remoteIpDetails (with ipAddressV4 and country) and remotePortDetails.

export.title: Exporting generated GuardDuty findings to Amazon S3 buckets
supports: GuardDuty retains the generated findings for 90 days.
Export settings are regional: they are configured in each Region where GuardDuty is used.
Archived findings, including new instances of suppressed findings, are not exported by default.
Updated active findings are exported at a set frequency: 15 minutes, 1 hour or 6 hours, with 6 hours the default.

Findings objects are written under a path of the form /AWSLogs/<account id>/GuardDuty/<Region>, and the S3 object is a UUID with the extension .jsonl.gz; the UUID is not the detector id or the finding id.
An administrator account's export includes the findings of its member accounts generated in the same Region.
export.not_supported_by_the_page_and_so_not_cla: the letter case of the keys inside an exported finding

aggregation.title: GuardDuty finding aggregation
supports: When GuardDuty detects new activity related to the same security issue, it updates the original finding with the latest details instead of creating a new one, aggregating it under the same finding id and increasing the Count.
An aggregated finding is updated with the latest occurrence, and older information such as a remote IP is replaced.
Which activity is aggregated into one finding and which creates a new one depends on the finding type.

suppression.title: Suppression rules in GuardDuty
supports: New findings that match a suppression rule are automatically archived; GuardDuty continues to generate them and marks them as archived.
Suppressed findings are not sent to Security Hub CSPM, Amazon S3, Amazon Detective or Amazon EventBridge.
Archived findings are kept for 90 days and are found through the service.archived criterion.

severity.title: Severity levels of GuardDuty findings
supports: The severity value lies between 1.0 and 10.0; Low is 1.0 to 3.9, Medium 4.0 to 6.9, High 7.0 to 8.9 and Critical 9.0 to 10.0.

guardduty-api.json.format: a GetFindings response with two findings, lowerCamelCase, one active and one archived
guardduty-api.json.schema_version: schemaVersion 2.0 as the fixture writes it (the page does not give a value)
guardduty-api.json.documentation: pages.finding, pages.service, pages.get-findings; checked against the live pages: yes, 2026-11-04

guardduty-export.jsonl.format: JSON Lines, one finding per line, with UpperCamelCase keys (the form the card uses; the export page does not say which form the export has, so the tool reads both): one finding id exported three times as it was updated, and one finding of another Region and account
guardduty-export.jsonl.documentation: pages.finding, pages.service, pages.export, pages.aggregation; checked: yes, 2026-11-04; the key case is the card's and is NOT confirmed by a page
